title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2. The 2-torsion E[2] is a Klein four-group V, and the four Weierstrass/branch points I of x: E → P^1 form a V-torsor. Grothendieck sets up a canonical, functorial dictionary for the exceptional homomorphism S_4 → S_3.

Step 1 (previous page and top of this one). G is an abstract group isomorphic to S_4. Let V be its maximal normal abelian subgroup, a 2-dimensional F_2-vector space. Then G/V ≅ GL(V) ≅ S_J, where J = V^* = V∖{0} (three elements). The set I_G of 3-Sylow subgroups (four of them) is a torsor under V acting by conjugation. Starting from a 4-set I, the map i ↦ S^+_{I∖{i}} (the Sylow fixing i) gives a bijection I ≅ I_{S_I}. In the other direction, the conjugation action gives G ≅ S_{I_G}. So I ↦ S_I and G ↦ I_G are quasi-inverse equivalences between the groupoid of 4-element sets and the groupoid of groups isomorphic to S_4.

Step 2. The elements of S_I are classified canonically.
(a) The identity.
(b) The 3 nonzero elements of V (double transpositions). They form one conjugacy class and correspond to Π_22(I), the partitions of I into two pairs.
(c) The 8 elements of order 3. They split into two packets of 4 according to their image among the two nontrivial elements of S_J^+ = A_3. Each packet is a V-torsor (by conjugation, or by left/right translation within the coset ρV). The whole set is canonically I × ω, where ω = orientations of V ≅ orientations of I. The map sends a 3-cycle ρ to its unique fixed point (equivalently the Sylow it generates) and to the orientation it induces (equivalently its image in A_3).
(d) The 6 transpositions, which map to the odd part S_J^-. They are in bijection with Π_2(I), the 2-element subsets of I. They also fibre over the 3 elements of V^*: τ_A pairs with τ_{A'} (A' = I∖A), the unique other transposition with τ_A τ_{A'} ∈ V^*.
(e) The 6 elements of order 4, in bijection with the 6 cyclic orders on I.

Step 3 (margins). Two geometric models are recorded:
- S_4 ≅ AGL(2, F_2), acting on the affine plane over F_2 with point set I. In this model V gives the nonzero translations (also the symmetries about centres); 3-cycles are 'rotations' with exactly one fixed point; transpositions are 'reflections' fixing an affine line.
- S_4 ≅ rotation group of the cube acting on its 4 long diagonals. In this model 3-cycles are vertex rotations, transpositions are edge rotations, 4-cycles are face rotations by π/2, and V gives the face rotations by π.

The next page continues: u ↦ u² gives a degree-2 map Circ(I) → V^*, recovering the cube structure. It also discusses the canonical isomorphism ω(I) ≅ ω(J) via signatures. All of this is bookkeeping to make the level-2 / cross-ratio (λ-invariant) symmetries of the Legendre family canonical rather than coordinate-dependent.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The counts match the conjugacy classes of S_4 (1+3+8+6+6 = 24).
The 8 three-cycles form a single conjugacy class in S_4. The 'two packets of 4' are the A_4-classes, i.e. the fibres over the two generators of A_3. Grothendieck's wording is consistent with this.
The machine transcription writes 'les deux éléments ±1 de S_J^+'. S_J^+ ≅ Z/3, so the intended reading is the two nontrivial elements ('≠1').

ideas.what: Canonical equivalence of groupoids between 4-element sets I and groups G ≅ S_4, via I ↦ S_I and G ↦ set of 3-Sylows, with the 3-Sylows forming a V-torsor
ideas.modern_name: Exceptional homomorphism S_4 → S_3 = GL_2(F_2) with Klein kernel; S_4 ≅ AGL(2,F_2); Aut(S_4) = Inn(S_4)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (19th century: Klein, Galois theory of the quartic and its resolvent cubic)

ideas.what: Canonical labelling of the conjugacy classes of S_I: double transpositions ↔ Π_22(I), 3-cycles ↔ I × orientations, transpositions ↔ Π_2(I), 4-cycles ↔ cyclic orders
Interpretation via the rotation group of the cube and via the affine plane over F_2 (translations, rotations, reflections)
ideas.modern_name: S_4 ≅ rotation group of the cube/octahedron ≅ AGL(2,F_2)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful, functorial ('canonical, choice-free') reorganisation of classical facts about S_4, its Klein subgroup and the cube. The style of making everything canonical is characteristic of Grothendieck and serves his study of level-2 structures on elliptic curves, but nothing here is new.
transcription_corrections: Section heading should read 'Éléments de 𝔖_I'.

In c): 'se répartissent en deux paquets de 4 qui sont des torseurs (à droite, ou à gauche) sous V, suivant les deux éléments ≠1 de 𝔖_J^+'. The transcription's 'générateurs en 4' should read 'paquets de 4', and '±1' should read '≠1' (likely).
In b): 'qui forment une orbite [sous] 𝔖_I'. The symbol read as 'Σ' is uncertain, possibly '⊐' or a stray mark.
Margin labels: '["rotations-sommets" des cubes]' next to c), '["rotations-arêtes" des cubes]' next to d), '["rotations-faces" des cubes]' next to e).
Margin next to d): '"réflexions" ayant une droite de pts fixes' (in the affine plane over F_2).
